summary:
# NOTES: Bertha's Visit to Her Uncle in England (Mrs. Marcet, 3 vols, 1830, Murray)

Source framing: journal of Bertha Montague, raised in Rio de Janeiro (Brazil) with mother (widow of Colonel Montague, d. in Brazil; mother too ill to travel). Bertha sent to uncle in England (Fernhurst, Gloucestershire area; forest of Deane). Journal sent to mother (Mamma) and sister Marianne. Ad: Editor selected extracts. Mother's brother = uncle (never named except "my uncle"). Aunt (unnamed). Cousins: Mary (delicate, timid, clear head, arithmetic, gardener), Caroline (handsomest, punctual, early riser, tenor voice), Wentworth (elder son, algebra, gardens), Frederick (younger son, mischievous, collector of insects, reads Frederick's "little garden boy" joke), Grace (youngest, little, obedient, uncle's playfellow). Cousin Hertford (travels Western Isles, Staffa, St Kilda, Lewis, etc.; letters quoted). Mrs. P---- (Gertrude P., née, ex-Jamaica; her narrative in Vol 2). Captain M. (of HMS Phaeton). Farmer Moreland & Dame Moreland. Mr. Biggs (gardener's friend/nurseryman). Mr. Lumley (= Fitzroy, the harvest-home gentleman, formerly "Fitzroy" of Strath-morton); Mrs. Lumley; Miss Lumleys (2 daughters). Mr. Benson (clergyman). Bessy Grimley & blind old man (basket-maker, lost sight in mines); Franklin (James, American farm, married Bessy). Madeleine & Bertram (Savoy; Newnham, Mrs. Ando). Miss Perceval (botanist). Mr. Maude / Miss Maudes (Elmore). Colonel Travers (ex-India; Ceylon stories). Mr. R-- (tabasheer). Mr. Scouler, Dr. Wells, etc. Canadian correspondent Mrs. * * * (Upper Canada letters). Lady Binning. Gardener (unnamed, valued).

Vol 1 (Phaeton voyage June–Falmouth 31 July 1829 approx; arrival Fernhurst Aug 3; ends with Oct 1829 Bertha's journal): sea birds (tropic-bird/phaeton, man-of-war bird, albatross, petrels, boobies), luminous sea animals, Gulf Stream explained by Captain, sea-weed & limpets, salt test with towel, flying fish, bonito, albacore, dolphin, grampus, Azores (Flores, Corvo), Cornish cliffs, Falmouth (St Mawes, Pendennis). Fernhurst: no slaves; Uncle's teachings on Sabbath, Scripture, Lapland reindeer/Iceland moss, harvest, Bessy Grimley story, Ker Porter Babylon/Tigris kelek, Ceylonese/Bedah story (Vol 2), Stockholm, Mont Grenier, Hertford letters, Lewis Druidical stone, Brazilian birds (baya, sociable grossbeak), cow instinct, mosses, Mr. R. Tabasheer etc.
Key: Gertrude P.'s narrative (Vol 2, 6 Feb entry), Nanina & Apakong rebellion in Jamaica, San Pedro plantation, Mr. Edward P., Mr. Crispin (old friend, Jamaica property gift), Phaëton to Brazil; Madeleine & Bertram; Canada letters (Mrs. *** at Cobourg/Loghouse). Vol 2 ends 1830-06? Actually Vol 2 ends with Canada extract 30 April/May 2 and Bertha's last Fernhurst-lapse; Vol 3 begins April 1 (1830).

Vol 2 selected events: Dec 1 pepper vine; Davy the blacksmith's horseshoe music; Passover (Dec 4); Juan Fernandez (Scouler); Bertha's garden; Christmas mummers; Ten words; Mrs. P's narrative in Vol 2 (6–8 Feb 1830? actually 8 Feb); Dormouse; Mirage letter; palimpsest; Titmouse; Swallow; Tabasheer; Mona/Wales in Vol 3.

Vol 3 selected: Apr 1 pear blossoms; Deuteronomy; trap rocks; Venice; Juan palm; Holyhead (last letter, June 23).

# Detailed anchor facts (use for specific Qs)

Key numbers/dates: Phaeton departs Rio ~June 1829; Captain M. kind; Falmouth 31 July; arrival Fernhurst 3 Aug; Bertha's garden begun ~Sept/Oct; Forest of Deane ~20 miles long, 10 broad; Staffa cave 227 ft long; 42 ft breadth; North Rona: 50 sheep, one family; Kilda ~100 people; Mont Grenier fall 1248, 5 parishes, St. André, 9 sq. miles, Abîmes de Myans; Babylon walls 60 miles, 350 ft high, 87 thick; Birs Nimrod; athelé tree. Potato introduced to England 1596 by Raleigh; potatoes carried to Persia by Sir John Malcolm ("Malcolm's plum", Abusheher). Locust swarm (Smyrna, 1811): 168,608,563,200,000 locusts; 4818 million cubic yards; 1030× Cheops pyramid; girdle 1 mile 1/8 wide. Mammoth Lena 1804 (Adams 1806). Sheep-shearing; Llangollen aqueduct 1000 ft, 20 piers 130 ft; Menai chain bridge (Bertha's sketch); Holyhead Stack light-house, 400 steps, rope bridge 100 ft. Penrhyn slate quarries (Bangor). Northwich salt mine. Kidderminster carpets; Shropshire inclined plane 350 yd, fall 70 yd, 21 locks replaced. Gloucester cathedral: nave length 1/12 mile, 200 ft high. Mrs. P's narrative: parents' house on Ulleswater; husband Edward P.; boys; Mr. Crispin; Jamaica San Pedro plantation; Nanina (faithful slave-girl, later freed, married); Apakong (Maroon descendant, insurgents); Haiti shipwreck; Phaëton to Brazil. Canada letters: Cobourg (Oct), Loghouse (Feb 24), Mr. * * * (husband), two/three children.

# Recurring characteristics
- Uncle: Sunday lectures on Scripture (Deuteronomy, Passover, Levitical/Patriarchal/Christian dispensations, Ten Words, Balaam, Moses' prophecies), science lectures (geology series, dew/frost, glass manufacture, coal, tides), gently teaches via questions; motto: "learn facts," "discrimination," "pleasure in doing."
- Aunt: practical charity, botany/zoology; "Bertha" kindnesses; Shakspeare debates.
- Bertha: asks questions, keeps journal, gardens (quarry garden, strawberries, budding roses, dahlias, hyacinths, carnation wire-worm salt dross; pond experiment with agapanthus/amaryllis/calla).
- Caroline & Wentworth: capping verses, genius debate (Cimabue, Canova, Chantrey, West, Mozart, Haydn, Denham/Swift).

Note: I have compacted from memory of the text; for exact quotes, re-read source.
